$comment: PR review risk tiering. Read by ~/.claude/hooks/pr-review-policy.sh.
Any file matching 'high' => HIGH (Gitar + CodeRabbit). All files matching 'low' => LOW.
Everything else => NORMAL (Gitar only). No match anywhere => NORMAL, deliberately.
This is the QuickFIX/n fork (branch fpsim). spec/ and DataDictionaries/ are HIGH even
though they look like data files: they drive DDTool code generation, and the generated
field set is an additive, name-keyed, processing-order-dependent SHARED namespace.
A dictionary edit can therefore change wire behaviour for versions it never mentions.
LOW justification for THIS repo: docs/ and upstream-findings/ are analysis notes -
neither is compiled, generated from, or shipped. Messages/, Fields/ and Tags.cs are
generated CODE and are NORMAL, never low.
Dependency manifests are deliberately NOT in 'high' and must not be added (estate rule,
what Dependabot edits, and dependency PRs are out of AI code review on both vendors:
CodeRabbit refuses bot authors outright and Gitar's bot review is switched off, because
reviewing every bump exhausts the allowance and starves the changes that need it. Listing
them HIGH would demand a reviewer that can never run - coverage on paper, none in fact. CI
plus Dependabot's own advisory data is what gates a bump. nuget.config, global.json, .npmrc
and Directory.Build.props stay HIGH: registry/feed and analyzer config, not bot-edited.
